t: Signing up and creating the account
s: How you create your login, and then the account that holds your venues together.
h: Your login The account The trial
b: Signing up has two parts. First you create your own login, then the account that holds your venues, your team and the daily report. You do not need a bank card. On the sign-in page, click the No account yet? Sign up. link. Type your email address in the Email field. Choose a password of at least 8 characters in the Password field, then type it again in the Password again field. Press the Sign up button. Under the button it says that by signing up you accept the terms of service and acknowledge the privacy notice. You can open both from there. On the Create your account page, type the name of the venue or the company in the Account name field. You can rename it later. Check the Time zone field. We fill it in from your browser, but you can change it. In the Language field, choose the language of your daily report. Press the Create account button. After that, the First steps guide opens by itself. It takes you through adding a venue and setting up the daily report. Tip: If a colleague invited you to an existing account, do not create a new one. Sign up from the invitation link, and you land in the right account straight away. A new account starts with a 14-day trial. What it includes, and where you see how many days are left, is in the article about the trial.

s: You find the venue on Google, add it, and a few minutes later you see its latest reviews.
h: How to add it What you see next What we download first If you get stuck If you want to pause a venue
b: The account owner adds venues. The first one in the First steps guide, the others on the Venues page, with the same card. Open the Venues page in the Account group of the menu. In a new account, the First steps guide opens by itself instead. On the Add venue card, type the venue's name, with the city if you like. For example: “Példa Bisztró Budapest”. Press the Search button. In the results, check the address and the number of reviews, so you are sure to pick your own venue. Press the Add button. The First download card shows how far the download has got. First it shows the review count and the average that Google displays, then how many reviews we have downloaded. The download usually takes a minute or two. Meanwhile you can go on to the next step of the guide. Until the first daily report is ready, the Today tab works from the downloaded reviews. It shows how many reviews we downloaded, their average, and how many negative reviews from the last 30 days are waiting for a reply. Meanwhile we write replies to the recent reviews that have none yet. You find those replies on the Replies tab. The venue's latest reviews, not its whole history. We do not write replies to the older reviews. You see them on the Reviews tab. The daily report does not count the older reviews of the first download as new. The first daily report arrives at the hour you set. If that hour has already passed today, it arrives tomorrow. If there are no results, add the city, or type the name exactly as it appears on Google. If a result says “Already on the list”, you have already added that venue. If your current plan has no room for another venue, the page says so. Then write to us. If the download fails, we try again in the morning. You do not need to do anything. Tip: Linking your Google Business Profile is a separate step. Downloading reviews does not need it. Posting replies does. See: Adding us as a manager on Google. On the Venues page, untick the Active box in the venue's row. We do not download the reviews of a switched-off venue, and it drops out of the daily report. Nothing is lost, and you can switch it back on at any time.

t: Adding us as a manager on Google
s: If you add our account as a manager on your Google Business Profile, we post the replies you approve.
h: The address you add On Google Checking Until it is linked Taking the access back
b: We download your reviews without it. Manager access is needed for two things. It lets us post your approved replies to Google, and it lets the Listing page see your Business Profile. The account owner takes these steps. Open the Venues page and press the Check connection button. If a venue is not linked yet, the Linking to Google Business Profile card appears. It shows the email address you need to add as a manager. Copy the address. Open your Google Business Profile with the Google account you manage it with as its owner. In the profile's settings, find the users, and add a new user with the address you copied. Choose manager as the role, and send the invitation. Google emails us an invitation. The link works from the moment we accept it. Go back to the Venues page and press Check connection again. Look at the Google connection column. If it says Linked for the venue, you are done. If it still says Not linked, try again later. If nothing changes then either, write to us with the Feedback button in the menu. Nothing stops. We still write the reply, you approve it, copy it with one button, and paste it in on Google yourself. See: Posting a reply by hand, without Google access. You can take the manager access back on your Google Business Profile at any time.

s: You set the hour the daily report arrives, and connect Telegram if you want it there too.
h: The time Connecting Telegram Without Telegram The other two destinations
b: Every day at the hour you set, the daily report sums up the previous 24 hours, venue by venue. You can always read it in the app, and we also send it to Telegram if you connect it. The account owner can change the settings. Open the Settings page. At the top it says what time the report goes out, and in which time zone. On the Account card, choose the hour in the Daily report hour field. Press the Save button at the bottom of the page. In a new account, the report goes out at 08:00 in the morning, in the account's time zone. On the Telegram destinations card of the Settings page, press the Connect button in the Daily report row. If you want the report for yourself, press the Open it on Telegram link, and start the chat in Telegram. If you want it in your team's group, add the BistroTech Telegram account to the group. The panel shows its name. Then send the command shown on the panel in the group. You can copy it with the Copy button. When the code arrives, the panel shows which chat sent it. If it is the right one, press the Yes, there button. The code is valid for 10 minutes. If it has run out, press Connect again. If you connect nothing, the report is still made at the hour you set. You read it on the Sent messages page, in the Account group of the menu. Such a report is marked “Here only. No Telegram chat is connected.” To have your phone tell you when it arrives, see: Putting it on your phone. Reports by email start later. You can already set the switches on the By email too card of the Settings page. The Marketing destination gets the weekly rank summary, and Alerts gets the alerts. You connect both the same way. See: Alerts. Tip: You can also ask questions in the daily report's chat. Write your question after the /kerdes command, for example: /kerdes what happened at Példa Bisztró this week. The assistant answers from your own reviews.

s: From your home screen, BistroTech opens like an app, and it can send you notifications.
h: On Android On iPhone Notifications on your phone
b: You do not download anything from an app store. You put BistroTech on your home screen from your phone's browser, and from there it opens without the browser bar. Open BistroTech in Chrome and sign in. If the Add to your home screen bar appears at the top of the page, press the Install button. Confirm the browser's question. If you hid the bar earlier, you can also install it from Chrome's menu. Open BistroTech in Safari and sign in. Open the Share menu. Choose Add to Home Screen, and confirm. Open the My login page: in the menu, click your own email address. On the Notifications on this device card, press the Turn on button, and allow it when the browser asks. Tick what we should tell you about: A low review arrived, The morning report is in. On iPhone, notifications only work from the BistroTech you put on the home screen. A notification goes to the device you turned it on for. You turn it on separately on each device. We tell you about a low review when the instant alert is on in Settings and a Telegram chat is connected. See: Alerts.

t: What the numbers in the daily report mean
s: What we count as new, what each venue's lines show, and what the parts at the end of the report mean.
h: What counts as new For each venue At the end of the report The analysis The same numbers on the Today tab
b: The daily report comes as two messages. The first holds the numbers, the second the analysis, if reviews with text arrived that day. A review is new when the guest posted it in the 24 hours before the report. Google sometimes releases a review late. Then the first report after it arrives counts it, up to seven days after it was posted. Every review is counted by exactly one report. If a report is made again, it gives the same number. If the guest rewrites the review, we do not count it again. A separate part shows the change, see: Changed and removed reviews. The number of new reviews and their average. The star breakdown, from five down to one. The venue's Google rating and its total number of reviews. A red mark if a one-star or two-star review arrived. Venues with no new review get one line each at the end of the list. Below them, the “Total” line gives the numbers for the whole account. “Unanswered negatives”: reviews of three stars or fewer, at most 14 days old, that have waited at least a day. We do not see a reply to them yet. The oldest comes first, and each has a link to the review. “No fresh data”: the venues where the download failed or was skipped. The next successful download makes up for them. If no new review arrived at any venue, the report flags it as a warning. At a smaller venue this is common, and it does not mean anything is wrong. If you connected Tripadvisor, a separate line shows the new reviews there. They are not in the Google numbers. The second message is made from the day's reviews with text. The “Mentions by name” part lists the staff guests named, and the “Themes” part what came up more than once. If no review with text arrived that day, this message is not sent. On the Today tab, The period in numbers card works from the same daily numbers. You choose the period with the Today, 7 days and 30 days buttons. The Full breakdown by star table shows the stars for each venue.

t: The extra report lines and the monthly summary
s: Four switches in Settings: three extra lines in the daily report, and a monthly summary.
h: Where to switch them The four switches The report's name In the weekly summary
b: The daily report can carry three lines on top of what it always carries. They appear only when they have something to say. In a new account, all four switches are on. Open the Settings page and find the Report card. Switch on or off what you want. Press the Save button at the bottom of the page. The account owner sets the switches. Negatives waiting for a reply, per venue: under each venue's line, we show how many one-star, two-star and three-star reviews are still waiting for a reply. We also show how long the oldest has waited. We only count the ones that arrived after we started watching the venue. Time of day line: if at least three negatives arrived in the day, and most of them fall in one part of the day, the report names that part. There are four: lunch, afternoon, evening and night. The time is when the guest wrote the review, not when they ate with you. Google removal line: if the review count Google shows has fallen by two or more since the previous reading, the report says by how much. We do not flag a fall of one, because that is Google's own churn. Monthly summary to the group: on the first of each month, a short text about the past month. We send it where the daily report goes on Telegram. If no Telegram chat is connected, you get no monthly summary either. On the same card, in The report's name field, you can give the report a name. It stands at the top of the daily report and the weekly summary, in capitals. Left empty, the name BistroTech goes there. The weekly summary's “This week” list is built partly from the same three signals. A line you switch off drops out of the weekly list too. See: The weekly summary.

s: Every Monday you get the past week, venue by venue, against the week before.
h: Which week What is in it The weekly rank summary
b: On Monday, shortly after the daily report, the weekly summary arrives. It goes where the daily report goes: to Telegram, or to the Sent messages page if no chat is connected. The summary looks at the last seven days, up to and including yesterday. We compare every number with the seven days before that. For each venue, the number of new reviews and the direction of the change against the week before. For each venue, the number of five-star, two-star and one-star reviews, and the weekly average. The totals for the whole account. The names mentioned most, venue by venue. The themes that kept coming back during the week. Your guests' language mix, when we know the language of enough reviews. The “This week” list, with at most three items. If part of the week has no data, the heading says how many days the summary was made from. If you watch search phrases on the Rank page, a second summary is made on Monday, about your positions on Google Maps. It goes to the Marketing destination on Telegram, and only if you connected it. See: Your rank on Google Maps and your competitors. You can read both summaries again on the Sent messages page, under the Weekly summary kind.

s: When we tell you something outside the daily report, and where the alert goes.
h: Instant alert on a low review Pattern alarm Error message
b: Outside the daily report, we send three kinds of alert to Telegram. All three go to the Alerts destination, so it is worth connecting that one too, on the Telegram destinations card of the Settings page. See: Setting up the daily report. Open the Settings page and find the Instant alert on a low review card. In the Alert when the review is at most field, choose the number of stars. If you do not want the alert, choose Off. In the two Quiet hours fields, set when we should stay quiet. Press the card's Save button. In a new account the setting is 2 stars. As soon as such a review reaches us, we tell you within fifteen minutes. What arrives during the quiet hours, we send together as soon as they end. If the Alerts destination is not connected, this alert goes to the daily report's chat. If neither is connected, we cannot tell you. During the day we watch for two patterns at each venue. One is several one-star reviews arriving in a short time. The other is several guests lowering an earlier rating within a few days. We only watch the Google reviews. We tell you about the same pattern once a day. This alert only goes to the Alerts destination. The alert can name who has to be told. You set that on the Settings page, in the Who to notify on an alert field. If several one-star reviews arrived at a venue within 24 hours, a warning card appears on the Today tab too. If the pattern looks suspicious, open a case for it, see: Disputing reviews with Google. If something fails on our side, a venue's download for example, the Alerts destination gets a short message. Usually there is nothing for you to do: the next scheduled run makes up for it. Tip: Your phone can tell you about a low review too. See: Putting it on your phone.

s: How to find every review of one venue, one star rating or one word.
h: Search Quick filters More filters A review's card Notes and who handles it
b: The Reviews tab shows every review we downloaded, newest first. At the top you find a search field and a few quick filters. Type a word in the search field, for example “goulash” or “waiter”. We search the text of the reviews. All: takes every filter off. Needs a reply: reviews of three stars or fewer that we do not see a reply to yet. 1 and 2 stars: the worst reviews. 5 stars: the best ones. All venues: here you pick one venue, if the account has several. All sites: here you choose between Google and Tripadvisor, if you connected Tripadvisor. Under More filters you can also filter by stars, reply, sentiment and text. You set the order here too: Newest first or Lowest rating first. The number of matches stands above the list. Tip: The filters are kept in the browser's address bar too. If you copy the address, your colleague opens the same list. The stars, the guest's name, the time and the language. The analysis: the sentiment, at most two themes and the staff named. A New mark if it arrived since your last visit. Whether it has a reply yet, and a link that opens the review on Google or on Tripadvisor. The Notes, owner link under the review opens the team's own part. In the Assigned to field, you choose which colleague handles it. Under Internal notes, you write what you know about the case, and save it with the Add button. Only the team sees the notes, never the guest. Colleagues with the viewer role can only read them.

s: What happens when a guest rewrites a review, or when Google takes one down.
h: If the guest rewrites it If Google takes a review down
b: A review can change after it is posted. The guest can rewrite it, and Google can take it down. We watch for both. On Google, a guest can write one review about a venue. If they rewrite it, Google sometimes gives it a new identifier. We still treat it as one review, and we do not count it again. On the Reviews tab you always see the latest version. We keep the old version too, and show the change from it. The “Changed reviews” part of the daily report lists what changed from what to what. For example from five stars to one, or that only the text changed. Lowered reviews come first, with their new text. The change is not counted again in the numbers. If several guests lower their rating at one venue within a few days, we send a pattern alarm. See: Alerts. Tip: You can also ask on the Assistant page which reviews changed in a given period. Google sometimes removes reviews, for example when they break a rule. We see this from the review count on your Business Profile going down. The daily report's “Google removal” line says so when the count has fallen by two or more since the previous reading. We do not flag a fall of one, because that is Google's own churn. From the count we cannot tell exactly which review has gone. You switch the line on and off on the Report card of the Settings page. See: The extra report lines and the monthly summary. If the fall looks suspicious to you, open a case for it on the Disputes page. See: Disputing reviews with Google.

s: If the venue is on Tripadvisor, we bring in its reviews there too, kept apart from the Google numbers.
h: Switching it on What changes then If something goes wrong Switching it off
b: You switch Tripadvisor on venue by venue. The account owner can do this. Open the venue's page on Tripadvisor and copy its address from the browser's address bar. The address starts like this: “tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-”. In BistroTech, open the Venues page and click the venue's name. On the Tripadvisor card, paste the address into the The venue's Tripadvisor address field. Press the Connect button. The first download brings up to 150 reviews from the last six months, and takes a few minutes. Meanwhile the card refreshes by itself. After that we refresh once a day, before the morning report. On the Reviews tab, Tripadvisor reviews get a mark of their own. With the All sites picker, you can ask for only them, or only the Google reviews. In the daily report, a separate line shows the new Tripadvisor reviews. They do not mix into the Google numbers. We write replies to these too. But we cannot post to Tripadvisor, so you copy the reply and post it from your Tripadvisor owner account. See: Posting a reply by hand, without Google access. Auto-answer never posts a reply to a Tripadvisor review by itself. If the download fails, the card shows the reason, and we try again the next morning. If the address is not a Tripadvisor restaurant page, the card says so, and nothing changes. You stop it with the Switch off button on the card. The reviews so far stay, and no new ones arrive.

s: You make a short link and a QR code, from which a guest can write a review on Google.
h: Making a link What the guest sees The rules the link keeps Printing Switching off and deleting
b: You can make a short link with a QR code for every venue. Whoever opens it sees the venue's name and a button to write a review on Google. If you connected Tripadvisor too, they can write one there as well. The account owner and the members can make links. Open the Venues page and click the venue's name. On the Ask for reviews card, type where the link will go, for example “table card”. Only you see this, the guest does not. Press the New link button. The Copy link button copies it, and you can send it in a message or a newsletter. The card shows how many times the link was opened in the last 30 days. Next to it you see the number of Google reviews for the same period. The two may move together, but that does not mean one causes the other. The guest sees a short page. We thank them for the visit and ask them to write how it was. The page speaks the language of the guest's phone: Hungarian, English, German, French, Italian or Spanish, and English for any other language. Apart from the language, every guest sees the same thing. We ask everyone the same way. We do not ask first whether they were happy. We promise nothing in return, no discount and no gift. Google forbids it and may remove reviews because of it. We do not ask the guest to name anyone, and there are no per-waiter codes. The printable card and the QR code download are coming soon. Until then you can try the link and share it, but its address will change later. So for now, do not print the QR code on the screen either. After Switch off, the link shows a page saying the link is no longer active. You can only delete a link that is switched off, with the Delete button. Deleting it also loses the count of opens.

s: You open a case on suspicious reviews and get a dated document for your report to Google.
h: When to open a case Opening a case The document Reporting to Google Afterwards
b: You find the Disputes page in the More group of the menu. The account owner opens and changes cases. When several one-star reviews arrived at a venue in a short time. When guests lowered an earlier rating afterwards. When Google took reviews off your venue's listing. When you want to report a single review. Press the New case button. The last 14 days list offers our alerts and the days the review count fell. If one fits, the Use this one button fills in the form with it. If you know about something we did not see, fill in the form by hand. The fields are Venue, What you are documenting, From this day and To this day. Press the Open the case button. In the list of cases, open the case with the Open link. The Open the document button opens the document in a new tab, and from there you can save it as a PDF with the browser's print. The Download as Markdown button gives it to you as a text file. The document holds the venue and the Business Profile id, the window, and the review count day by day. Next to that, the one-star reviews against the venue's previous 90 days, and every review in the window, word for word. At the end come the changed reviews, our alerts and Google's own pages, with the date we read them. The document does not claim the reviews are fake. Whether a review comes down is Google's decision alone. You send the report yourself. At Google, you can report the reviews from your Business Profile or from Google's Reviews Management Tool. You have to say which policy they break. After a refusal you can appeal once, and one appeal takes at most ten reviews. Warning: If somebody asks for money to take the reviews down, do not pay and do not answer. Google keeps a separate report form for this. In the case's What Google said part, fill in the Status, Google case reference and Notes fields. Then press the Save button. When you set it to filed, we record today's date. The notes go onto the document too. Google gives no deadline for a removal.

s: How you look through the ready replies and approve them.
h: Step by step
b: We write a reply to every new review. Until you approve it, it goes nowhere. This is how you look through them. Open the Replies tab. Next to the tab you can see how many replies are waiting. The worst review comes first. Read it. Below it is the ready reply. Edit it if you need to. With the Rewrite buttons you can ask for it shorter, warmer or firmer, or switch it to formal or informal address. You can restore the original at any time. Press Approve. You can undo it for eight seconds. If you have added us as a manager on Google, we post the reply within a few minutes. If not, you copy it with the Copy and open Google button and paste it on Google. Tip: Faster with a keyboard. A approves, S skips, J and K move, E edits, O opens Google, U undoes. A skipped review stays without a reply. You can still find it later under Reviews.

s: How you fit the replies to your own voice with the rewrite buttons, the voice notes, the rules and the sign-off.
h: The rewrite buttons The voice The rules What we always keep to
b: We write the replies to your settings, always in the guest's language. If the guest only left stars, in the account's language. On the Replies tab there are five buttons under the reply: Shorter, Warmer, Firmer, Formal and Informal. One press is one rewrite. The new text takes the place of the old one. The Back to the previous text link gives you back the text from before the rewrite. The Restore original link gives you back the first version we wrote. A rewritten reply also goes out only when you approve it. If you ask for many rewrites within an hour, rewriting pauses for a while. Meanwhile you can still edit the text by hand. Open the Settings page and find the Reply voice card. In the Voice field, write how the replies should sound: how to address the guest, what to avoid, how to sign off. Press the Save button at the bottom of the page. You can also give a single venue its own additions. On the Venues page, click the Voice notes link in the venue's row. On the Reply rules card of the Settings page, you set a few hard rules. The card has its own Save button. Form of address: As the guest wrote (polite when unclear), Always formal or Always informal. Sign-off at the end of a reply: if you leave it empty, the venue's name ends the reply. You can override it for each venue on the Venues page, in the Sign-off at the end of replies field of the Voice notes panel. Never write: words separated by commas. We catch other forms of the words too. If a reply would still contain one of them, it is not made. At most this many words: by default 70 words for a positive review, 120 for a negative one. The rules apply from the next review. We do not rewrite replies that are already written. The account owner sets the voice and the rules. We never promise a refund, a discount, free food or any other compensation. We never put a phone number, an email address or a link in a reply. On a negative review we apologise once, we do not argue, and we do not blame the guest.

s: Switched on, good reviews get their reply by itself, and nobody reads it first.
h: Turning it on What it means If you extend it to lower reviews Turning it off In the subscription
b: By default you approve every reply before it goes out. Automatic answering takes this over from you, from a star rating upwards. It is off by default, and only the account owner can turn it on. Open the Settings page and find the Automatic answering card. Tick the Automatic answering on box. Choose the threshold. By default the field says Answer automatically from 4 stars up. Press the Save button at the bottom of the page. Replies to reviews at or above the stars you set do not wait for approval. We post them to Google within a few minutes, and nobody reads them first. Replies to lower reviews still wait for you on the Replies tab. Replies posted this way are marked “automatic” in the list and in the history. It only applies to Google reviews. Replies to Tripadvisor reviews always wait for your approval. It also needs the Reply writing on box ticked on the Replies card. We can only post the reply where you added us as a manager on your Google Business Profile. Elsewhere the reply is written, but you have to paste it in. See: Adding us as a manager on Google. Warning: If you set the threshold to three stars or lower, lower reviews get a reply by itself too. That reply appears on your own Google Business Profile, where your guests see it, and nobody reads it first. The Settings page says this on the card too, when you pick such a threshold. A bad reply to a negative review is public. It is worth trying out first how your replies sound, by approving them yourself. See: Rewriting and the reply rules. Untick the Automatic answering on box and press the Save button. The replies already posted stay on Google. Every new reply waits for your approval again. The Activity page records turning it on and off. On the Subscription page, auto-answer is listed as an add-on. Its price has not been announced yet.

t: Posting a reply by hand, without Google access
s: If you have not added us as a manager, you copy the ready reply with one button and paste it in on Google yourself.
h: Step by step If you have no time now For a Tripadvisor review Worth knowing
b: If we have no manager access to a venue's Google Business Profile, we cannot post the reply. We still write it, and you approve it. You do the pasting. On the Replies tab, approve the reply with the Approve button. The reply is ready panel appears. Press the Copy and open Google button. The reply goes to the clipboard, and the review opens on Google in a new tab. On Google, reply to the review: paste the text and send it. If we have no link to the review, the panel shows the Copy reply button instead. Then find the review in your Google Business Profile. Press the Later button. The reply waits on the Replies tab, in the Approved, not yet posted list, marked “post it by hand”. You can carry on from there at any time, with the Copy reply button and the Open on Google link. We cannot post to Tripadvisor. There the Copy and open Tripadvisor button appears, and you post the reply from your Tripadvisor owner account. We do not see that you posted the reply by hand. So the reply stays on the approved list, and the review still looks unanswered to us. If you do not want to post replies by hand, add us as a manager. See: Adding us as a manager on Google.

s: The Analysis tab shows what keeps repeating in what guests write, and how your venues compare side by side.
h: The main numbers The two charts Themes Staff mentions Venue comparison
b: The Analysis tab shows the numbers for a period, venue by venue. You choose the period at the top: 7 days, 30 days or 90 days. New reviews and Average of new reviews: the reviews that arrived in the period. 1-star or 2-star share: of the new reviews. Unanswered negatives: three stars or fewer, with no owner reply. Reviews analysed: what percentage of the new reviews we have analysed so far. Google rating over time: per venue, from the daily check. Click a venue's name to hide or show its line. New reviews per day: all venues together. Under both, the Show as table link shows the same in numbers. From the reviews with text, we read out what they are about, for example the service, the waiting or the prices. Under Themes there are two lists: What guests praise and What guests complain about. Each holds the ten most frequent themes. A review counts a theme once. Complaint: a review with a negative sentiment, or of three stars or fewer. Praise: a review with a positive sentiment, or of four stars or more. For each theme you see at which venues it came up most. Every theme gets one name, so you can compare themes across venues and languages. This table shows the staff guests named, spelled the way the guests wrote them. A mention is positive when it is in a four-star or five-star review. It is negative in a review of three stars or fewer. You see the details on the Recognition page, see: Recognition and staff mentions. The last table puts your venues side by side. The columns: new reviews, average, one-star and two-star reviews, unanswered negatives, the Google rating now, change and total reviews. The change is the difference between the first and the last daily check of the period.

t: What guests write about each dish
s: The Dishes page shows which dishes guests mention at each venue, and in what kind of review.
h: The table Sorting As the guest wrote it If the table is empty
b: You find the Dishes page in the More group of the menu. It shows what guests name from the menu, venue by venue. You choose the period at the top: 30 days or 90 days. Every row is one dish at one venue. The Mentions column shows how many reviews named the dish. The Positive and Negative columns show in how many reviews it was spoken of well, and in how many badly. The Average is the star average of the reviews that named the dish. Click a heading to sort the table. Sorted by dish, a dish's venues sit next to each other, so you see where it turns out better. Where the same dish sits far apart at two venues, there is something to look at in the kitchen. Dishes appear as guests wrote them, in their own language. We do not translate them, and we do not match them to your menu. “Gulyás”, “goulash” and “gulasch” are three separate rows. We collect the dishes from the analysed reviews, shortly after a review reaches us. We do not analyse older reviews, so in a new account's first days there are few dishes on the list.

s: Who guests name, and how you fold the different spellings of one person's name together.
h: The table Name spellings Download Where else you see the names
b: You find the Recognition page in the More group of the menu. It shows the names guests wrote in their reviews, on a row of their own for each venue. You choose the period at the top: 7 days, 30 days or 90 days. Mentions shows how many reviews named the person. The Positive and Negative columns are the sentiment of the review the name appeared in. Not of the sentence about the person. The Other column holds neutral reviews and reviews not analysed yet. The What guests wrote button lets you read the mentions themselves. This list is for saying thank you, not for appraising anybody. The negative column is shown, but nothing ranks by it. Guests spell the same person several ways. On the Name spellings card you say which spelling means whom. Type the name in the The name to show in the list field, for example “Roland”. Type the spelling in the How guests write it field, for example “Roli”. Press the Add button. The list then folds them into one row. The account owner manages the name spellings. The Download as a spreadsheet button saves the list to a file, filtered and sorted as it stands on the screen. The daily report's analysis lists the staff mentioned, by name. The weekly summary carries the names mentioned most. On the Today tab, a card can also tell you when someone was praised several times this week.

t: Your rank on Google Maps and your competitors
s: You see where you stand in the Maps results for a search, and how the nearby restaurants are doing.
h: The search phrase and the starting point Adding a phrase The table of positions Competitors The weekly rank summary
b: You find the Rank page in the More group of the menu. The account owner adds search phrases and competitors. The search phrase is what a guest would type into Google Maps, for example “goulash budapest”. The starting point is a point on the map we measure the search from. We need it because Google puts the places near the searcher first. If you have no phrase yet, press the Add the first phrase button. After that you work on the New search phrase card. In the Search phrase field, type what a guest would search for. In the Name of the starting point field, give the point a name, for example “Deák tér”. Open Maps with the Open Google Maps to find coordinates link. Right-click the point a guest would search from, and copy the two numbers. Paste them into the Latitude (lat) and Longitude (lng) fields. You can also paste both at once into the first field. Press the Add phrase button. We measure once every morning, so a new phrase's result appears after the next morning run. You can have at most 30 active phrases at a time. For each phrase you see the position, the change over 7 days and the day it was measured. If the venue is not in the top 20, we say so. The History button shows the earlier measurements. Switch off leaves the phrase out of the morning run, and the earlier data stays. The Competitors board is at the bottom of the Rank page. It shows your venue next to up to five nearby places. You see their rating, how many reviews they have, how many they gained, and the position they held on your searches. Press the Add a competitor button. The list holds the places that came up for your phrases in the last 30 days. Press the Add button next to the one you want to watch. Switch on Daily competitor watch. While the watch is off, we look nothing up, and the board shows the earlier measurements. Switched on, every morning we check the rating and the review count of the places you added. The Remove button takes a place off the board, and its earlier measurements stay. On Monday a summary of your positions is made too. It goes to the Marketing destination on Telegram, if you connected it. See: The weekly summary.

s: You can ask about your own reviews and numbers, and the assistant shows what it answered from.
h: Asking What it can do for you On Telegram
b: You find the Assistant page in the More group of the menu. It answers from your own account's data: the reviews, the daily numbers, the replies written, the themes and the positions. Where there is no data, it says so. Press the New question button, or pick one of the suggested questions, for example “What happened this week?” Type the question and press the Send button. Enter sends it too, and Shift with Enter starts a new line. Above the answer sit the rows it worked from: reviews, daily numbers, names, themes. So next to every number you see what it came from. There is a set number of questions a day, and the page says how many you have used today. Conversations are kept, and you can carry on with any of them from the Conversations list. The assistant can approve or skip a reply, and post one you have already approved to Google. It only does this when you asked for it in your own message. It works through your own login, so what you may not do, it may not do either. It does not rewrite the reply's text. If you want to change it, you do that on the Replies tab. It can write a suggestion for the listing, but it changes nothing on Google by itself. The suggestion waits for your decision on the Listing page. In the daily report's chat you can also ask with the /kerdes command: write the question after the command. There the assistant answers from the data of the last 30 days. Tip: On the Settings page, in the What the assistant should know about your venues field, you can give the venues' old names or nicknames. Then it understands the question even when guests or colleagues call a venue something else.

s: The Listing page shows what your Google Business Profile says about you, what has gone stale on it, and what we suggest.
h: What you see for each venue The suggestions Writing to Google
b: You find the Listing page in the More group of the menu. It only works for the venues where you added us as a manager on your Google Business Profile. See: Adding us as a manager on Google. Last read: when we last read the listing. Description: how many characters long it is. Opening hours: whether they are published. Special hours in 30 days, Photos and Open suggestions. Reviews mentioning hours: how many reviews mentioned the opening hours in the last 30 days. We do not read the listing on our own. The account owner starts it with the Read the listing button, and then we update the suggestions. The suggestions come from the numbers we hold. We make one when guests found the door locked while the listing said the venue was open. Also when a public holiday is coming with no special hours, when the description is short or old, or when there are few photos. From the week's good reviews we also suggest a weekly post. We only write text for the weekly post. For the others you see what the listing says now, and the signal behind it. We do not guess your opening hours. You decide with the Approve and Drop it buttons. The account owner can do this. Writing to Google is not switched on yet. An approved suggestion stays, and the card says it has not gone out. Nothing goes from this page to Google today.

s: You bring your colleagues into the account with an invite link or by email address.
h: Invite link Inviting by email address Pending invitations Inviting a viewer
b: The account owner invites colleagues on the Team page. You find the page in the Account group of the menu. On the Create an invite link card, choose in the Role field whether they will be a Member or an Owner. Press the Create link button. Copy the link with the Copy link button. Do it now, because we cannot show it again later. Send it to your colleague in a message. The link works for seven days, and it can be used to join once. On the link, your colleague sees the account's name and their role. If they have no login yet, they sign up with the Sign up button. If they have one, they sign in with the I have an account, sign in button. Then the Join account button puts them in the account. If your colleague already has a BistroTech login, you can also invite them by their email address. On the Invite someone card, type their address in the Email address field, and choose their role. Press the Invite button. Tell them to sign in. The next time they sign in, they are in the account. If your colleague has no login yet, use the invite link. Invitations not used yet stand in the Pending invitations list, with their expiry date. The Revoke button cancels any of them. An invitation is for the owner or the member role. If you want someone to be a viewer, invite them as a member. When they have joined, change their role to Viewer on the Team page. See: Roles and access per venue.

s: Who can see and do what in the account, and how you limit a colleague to a few venues.
h: The three roles Changing a role Access per venue Removing and leaving Activity
b: Everyone on the account has a role. You manage roles and access on the Team page, in the Account group of the menu. Owner: sees and does everything. Invites and removes people, adds and switches off venues, changes the settings, and picks the package. Member: sees every page and can work on the replies: approve, skip, rewrite. Cannot change the account settings. Viewer: sees everything, but changes nothing. The owner changes the role on the Team page, in the colleague's row, in the Role column. The last owner cannot be removed, and their role cannot be changed. Make someone else an owner first. On the Team page, in the colleague's row, press the Edit link in the Venue column. Untick the All of them box, and tick the venues they may see. Press the Save button. Someone who does not see every venue sees only their own venues' reviews and replies. Not the account's totals, the team or the activity log. The owner always sees every venue. The owner takes a colleague off the account with the Remove button in their row. After that, the colleague has no access to the reviews. You leave yourself with the Leave this account link. An owner can invite you again later. The Activity page shows who did what in the account: the replies, the changes to the team and the venues, the settings and the invitations. With the buttons at the top you can filter, for example to the Replies or the Team area.

s: If you run several accounts, the Group page shows their numbers in one table and writes a weekly summary about them.
h: Creating a group The account's consent What the group sees Weekly summary about the group Deleting a group
b: One account can hold several venues, and that needs no group. A group is for when you have several separate accounts, one per company for example, and want to look at them together. Open the Group page in the Account group of the menu. On the New group card, fill in The group name field and press the Create the group button. In the Accounts part, choose the account from the Account to add list, and press the Add an account button. You can only add an account you own. Every account decides on its own Settings page, on the Group sharing card, whether it shares its summary. The account owner chooses between the Share it and Do not share buttons. The group sees nothing of an account that does not share. The Per account table gives every account one row. In it: the new reviews, the average, the negatives waiting for a reply, the changed reviews and the movement in rank. You choose the period with the 7 days and 30 days buttons. The group only sees counts and averages. No review, no guest name and no reply. On Monday morning a summary is made about the group too, with the most important things to do. If you fill in the Telegram chat id field on the Group settings card, we send it there. If it stays empty, you read it under Latest weekly summary. You see the chat's id on an account's Settings page, after you have connected the same chat to that account. First take the accounts out of the group with the Remove it button. Then, on the Group settings card, press Delete the group, and then Delete it. The accounts, the venues and the reviews stay untouched.

s: On the My login page you change your password, sign out of your other devices, and turn on two-step sign-in.
h: Two-step sign-in Changing your password Signing out of other devices
b: The My login page belongs to your own login, not to the venues' account. It opens when you click your own email address in the menu. Besides the password, you need a six-digit code from your phone's authenticator app, for example Google Authenticator. Even if your password leaks, nobody can sign in to your account with it. On the Two-step sign-in card, press the Turn on button. Scan the code that appears with the authenticator app, or type the key in by hand. Type the app's six-digit code and press the Check and turn on button. From then on, we ask for the code after the password when you sign in. If the code is not accepted, check that your phone's clock is accurate. You turn it off with the Turn off button, which also needs a fresh code. Warning: If you lose the phone with the authenticator app, you cannot sign in by yourself. Then only we can turn off two-step sign-in. Save the key in a second place too, for example in a password manager. On the Password card, type your current password in the Current password field. Type the new one in the New password and New password again fields. It must be at least 8 characters. If you want to sign out of your other devices too, tick the Also sign me out on other devices box. Press the Change password button. If you lost your phone, or left BistroTech open on a shared computer, you can sign out of every other device. Press the Sign out on all other devices button on the Other devices card. This device stays signed in.

t: Downloading your data and deleting the account
s: You download the data of the account or of your own login, and if you need to, you delete a venue, the account or your login.
h: The account's data Your own data Deleting a venue Deleting the account Deleting your login
b: You can download the data at any time. Deleting has three levels: a venue, the account, and your own login. The account owner downloads the data at the bottom of the Settings page, on the Download the account's data card. All data (JSON): the venues, the reviews with their analysis, the replies and the settings, in one file. Reviews as a spreadsheet (CSV): only the reviews, as a table. Excel set to Hungarian opens it directly. On the My login page, the Download my data button gives you your login's data. It holds your email address, the day you signed up, your accounts and the date you accepted the terms. On the Venues page, click the Voice notes link in the venue's row. Open the Delete the venue part, and type the venue's name. Press the Delete for good button, and confirm. Every review, reply and statistic of the venue is deleted for good. If you only want a pause, switch it off with the Active box instead: then nothing is lost. At the bottom of the Settings page, on the Delete the account card, type your password and the account's name. Press the Delete the account button, and confirm. We mark the account for deletion. The daily report stops at once, and the account disappears for everyone on the team. For 30 days you can restore it on the My login page, on the Accounts awaiting deletion card, with the Restore button. After that it is deleted for good. Warning: If you want to keep the account's data, download it first. After the final deletion we cannot give it back. The Delete my login card of the My login page deletes your own login, not the venues' account. If there is an account you are the only owner of, first make someone else an owner, or delete that account. Type your password, and type “DELETE” in the field. Press the Delete my login button, and confirm. Your login is deleted at once and for good.

s: You choose how BistroTech looks for you, and which language you see it in.
h: Where you set it Three steps, in order Light or dark In the Glass style only The language
b: Everyone sets the appearance for themselves, and the rest of your team sees their own. Your choice belongs to your login, so it opens the same way on your other devices. On the Appearance card of the Settings page. Every change shows at once, with nothing to save. Style: the shapes. Pop: thick outlines, hard shadows, colour blocks. Glass: frosted panels over a soft colour glow. Classic: calm, thin rules, paper white. Colours: only the colours of the chosen style appear. Pop has Lemon, Aperol, Matcha, Gelato, Balaton and the dark Midnight. Glass has Market, Aperol, Gelato, Balaton, Matcha, and the dark Neon and Paprika. Classic has Classic and Classic night. Font: the face of the headings and the numbers, from the style's own choice. The text face is the same in every style. The default is the Pop style with automatic colours and Space Grotesk. Light, Dark or Automatic. Automatic follows your device's setting: in Pop you see Lemon by day and Midnight at night. The Glass switch: Off, On the menu or On the cards too. Beside it, the Blur and Opacity sliders. Back to the default restores Pop, automatic colours and Space Grotesk. You set the language of the pages with the Language menu: Magyar or English. This is your own setting too. The language of the daily report is separate. It comes from the Language field of the Account card on the Settings page, and it applies to everyone in the account.

s: There are three packages, charged per venue per month. We will publish the prices soon.
h: The three packages The band Add-ons Asking for a quote Billing details and invoices Usage
b: You see the packages on the Subscription page, in the Account group of the menu. You also get there from the Plan card of the Settings page. The account owner can pick a package. The cards of the Starter, Analyst and Full packages show what each contains. Monitoring, the daily report and the written replies are in all three. The price is per venue per month, before VAT. The prices have not been announced yet, so every package says “Price soon”. You do not choose the band: it comes from the number of active venues on the account. There are three bands: one venue, two to nine, and ten or more. Auto-answer can be added to any package. Listing care and Competitor benchmark have no price yet, so they say “Coming”. Pick the package with the Choose this button, and tick the add-ons. Press the Request a quote button. We record what you picked. Nothing is paid here for now. On the Billing details card you enter who we invoice: company name, tax number, address, and the email address for invoices. The Invoices list is at the bottom of the page. We do not invoice during the trial. At the bottom of the Settings page, the Usage card shows counts. You see how many reviews we fetched, and how many count checks, analysis runs and messages sent there were. For this month, last month and the last six months. We show no price and no cost here.

s: A new account runs free for 14 days, without a bank card, on your own venues' real reviews.
h: What you get Where you see how far you are After the trial
b: A new account starts with a 14-day trial, counted from when you create the account. You need no bank card for it, and there is no minimum term. During the trial the full base package runs, on your own venues' real reviews. We download the reviews, write the replies, and the daily report is made every day. We do not invoice during the trial. During the trial you can add a limited number of venues. If you reach the limit, the page says so. If you need more, write to us. At the top of the Settings page, the Plan card shows your current plan and the days left. It gives the end of the trial in your own time zone. In the last days, a marker also appears in the menu and takes you to the Settings page. The rules for after the trial will be here soon. The packages are covered in Packages and billing.
